contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-oxxo-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-oxxo-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-oxxo.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo describes a single-use cash voucher for Mexican customers in MXN, 10–10,000 MXN, for eligible CA, MX, SG and US Stripe accounts and separately named private-preview locations, described in the headline as the EEA and UK. It covers merchant and Connect platform or marketplace accounts, B2B and B2C, and domestic or cross-border business coverage with Mexican customers. Access is provisional and may be reviewed after activation. Prohibited MCCs cannot use OXXO and restricted MCCs may qualify but require additional information at account creation. Standard Stripe website requirements still apply (new raw lines 9-13 and 19-81). At checkout, the customer provides both name and email before receiving a voucher with a 32-digit transaction reference. The Stripe-hosted voucher page and optional payment-instruction email show the OXXO transaction number and the merchant-of-record business name in place of a statement descriptor. In Connect the merchant of record can be the platform or a connected account. The customer pays cash at an OXXO store and gets a cashier receipt as immediate proof for the customer, separate from Stripe's payment confirmation (new raw lines 140-160). Stripe issues payment_intent.requires_action when the voucher is created and payment_intent.succeeded after the store payment is processed, with confirmation by the next business day. The overview lists settlement up to T+4, with Tuesday through Thursday payments settling the following Monday and Friday through Monday payments settling the following Wednesday (new raw lines 13-23 and 138-160). Its PaymentIntent voucher default is five days, customizable from one to seven. Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents are listed, with Payment Element and in-app support and Express Checkout Element, SetupIntents, setup_future_usage, recurring payments, native refunds and standard disputes excluded (new raw lines 82-137). The May 7 overview and source-stripe-oxxo.md retain MX-only merchant wording and same-next-business-day confirmation with settled funds alongside May standard payout language. They preserve the cash voucher, MXN range and refund limits (old raw lines 8-20, 34-68 and 98-117). The current summary also overstates unconditional Connect eligibility and still lists four historical categories without the new detail.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/oxxo November's substantive additions include expanded and provisional merchant eligibility, a detailed prohibited/restricted MCC table, five-day PaymentIntent voucher default, explicit payment events and T+4 weekday settlement, expanded feature and UI limits and voucher display identifiers (new raw lines 9-81 and 82-160). Reordered sections, removal of diagrams and old quickstart/sample links and the separately captured November acceptance variant index affect presentation or navigation. Preserve May 7 account scope, four listed categories, payout wording and Checkout payment-only mode in source-stripe-oxxo.md (old raw lines 34-68, 70-96 and 110-117). The November private-preview table includes CH while the headline says EEA and UK. The May acceptance guide remains dated to MX businesses for its Checkout and Checkout Sessions Elements paths, whereas November overview supports four standard account locations and private preview. Keep reciprocal warnings across overview, acceptance, concept and index. May acceptance lines 103-107, 1368-1394 and 2191-2193 give a three-day default on both Checkout Sessions and PaymentIntent forms. November overview line 13 gives five days on PaymentIntent with the same 1–7 day custom range. The November acceptance index gives no new default. Distinguish the expires_after_days request option from the expires_after response timestamp in the May acceptance guide at lines 208-215. Its illustrative expiry time is 23:59 America/Mexico_City. May overview joins confirmation and settled funds and separately lists standard payout timing (old raw lines 8-10 and 34-36). May acceptance lines 1474-1487 and 2294-2307 say funds are not immediate and scope the success webhook to the next business day, excluding Mexican holidays. November separates next-business-day confirmation from settlement up to T+4, with Tuesday–Thursday to following Monday and Friday–Monday to following Wednesday (new raw lines 13-23). Voucher issuance, receipt, Stripe success, settlement and arrival in the merchant bank account are distinct. May Checkout Session completion marks voucher creation. Await asynchronous paid or failed events to know the outcome (May acceptance lines 172-194). Checkout sends the customer to Stripe's hosted voucher page, and mobile can open that hosted voucher URL in an in-app webview (new raw lines 142-160 and May acceptance lines 172-174). The November voucher hub's API grid at lines 37-46 lists no required redirect for the payment method. Its label does not prevent Checkout from routing a customer to a hosted voucher for display. The May Direct API browser flow is the specific legacy route and uses stripe.confirmOxxoPayment with the PaymentIntent client secret to open a voucher modal (May acceptance lines 2077-2083 and 2244-2266). The collected-data variant requires both first and last name and email, correcting the email-only wording in the acceptance summary at line 23 and Cash Vouchers concept at line 107. The separately captured November Stripe.js reference specifies an existing PaymentMethod by ID, and permits a call without additional data when the PaymentMethod is already attached (Stripe.js reference lines 14-17, 41-53 and 61-79). These UI and API choices display or submit the voucher without confirming its cash payment.
